newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Bankers Trust NZ buys broker Doyle Paterson Brown.
newsitem.headline: Bankers Trust NZ buys broker Doyle Paterson Brown.

text.p: Bankers Trust New Zealand Ltd (BTNZ) said on Wednesday it had agreed to buy New Zealand stockbroker Doyle Paterson Brown Ltd.
BTNZ did not annnounce an acquisition price in a statement released by BT Australia in Sydney.

"The acquisition of DPB to BT's existing strengths, represents a real advantage for clients of Bankers Trust Australia. It provides them with immediate access to a larger distribution network and enhanced region-wide research capabilities," Bankers Trust Investment Bank head Gavin Walker said in the statement.
"As the Australian and New Zealand markets continue to integrate, it is important to be able to offer clients research with a substantial regional capability," Walker said.
The DPB acquisition would boost BT's global presence in London and New York in particular, BT said.
Sources told Reuters in New Zealand on Tuesday that BTNZ, a unit of Bankers Trust New York, would announce the purchase of DPB on Wednesday.
Walker said many industry sectors, such as airlines, brewing and forestry operated on a Australia-New Zealand basis and many stocks were listed on exchanges in both countries.
"We can now provide a more complete coverage of these sectors and stocks," he said.
Bankers Trust New Zealand chief executive Rob Morrison said the acquisition of DPB's equity reserach and distribution skills was an important addition to BTNZ.

"An equity specialist like DPB supplements BTNZ's existing strengths which include wholesale treasury operations, wholesale and retail funds management and corporate finance," Morrison said in the Sydney statement.
BT said no changes were envisaged to the business and staff numbers, but the Doyle Paterson Brown brand would be phased out and replaced by BT Securities (NZ) Ltd.
A BT spokesman told Reuters the purchase price would not be revealed.
DPB had about 10 percent of equities trading market share in New Zealand and had been in the top five brokers since 1989, the spokesman said.
The spokesman said there were no plans to move DPB from Wellington to BTNZ's main offices in Auckland.
"It gives BT a presence in Wellington," the spokesman said.
He said FR Partners, a subsidiary of unlisted merchant bank Fay Richwhite, had owned 24 percent of DPB.
